transcript.content: You are helping a patient respond to a health insurance denial. Answer precisely and only from evidence you actually retrieve. If you cannot find the governing policy, say so plainly rather than naming a document you are unsure of.

NOTICE OF ADVERSE BENEFIT DETERMINATION

Date of notice: 2026-08-23
Member: Harper Grant
Member ID: W740585624
Plan: Blue Cross and Blue Shield of North Carolina (Commercial/ACA), state of North Carolina

Dear Harper,

We reviewed the prior authorization request submitted by your provider for the following service:

    Requested service: Bunion surgery (hallux valgus)
    Procedure code (CPT): 28296

After review, this request is DENIED. Reason for determination: the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity.

This determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria. You have the right to appeal this decision. Your appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of this notice (by 2027-02-19).

Reference number: POC-BA397EFDB1-13824


---

Above is a denial letter. Using web search as needed:

1. Identify the payer's governing medical policy for the denied procedure --
   the specific document containing the medical-necessity criteria this payer
   applies to this CPT code.
2. Give its title, policy number, URL, and effective or last-revised date.
3. Quote the medical-necessity criteria the patient must address.
4. State the appeal deadline.
5. State where and how to submit the appeal.

If no such document is publicly available, say so explicitly and explain how
the patient can obtain the criteria that were applied to them.

{"url": "https://www.bcbsnc.com/providers/policies-guidelines-codes/commercial/administrative/updates/medical-necessity", "final_url": "https://www.bcbsnc.com/providers/policies-guidelines-codes/commercial/administrative/updates/medical-necessity", "http_status": 200, "content_type": "text/html; charset=utf-8", "login_wall": false, "blocked": false, "blocked_reason": null, "error": null, "text": "Medical Necessity | Blue Cross NC lh-theme primary-extra-dark lh-content-width xl lh-padding-top sm lh-padding-bottom sm Medical Necessity lh-theme primary-extra-dark lh-content-width md lh-padding-top none lh-padding-bottom md Commercial Medical Policy lh-theme primary-extra-dark lh-content-width md lh-padding-top none lh-padding-bottom md Origination Date: 09/1999 Last Review Date: 11/2025 lh-theme primary-extra-dark lh-content-width md lh-padding-top none lh-padding-bottom md lh-spacing extra-tight Description of Service This is a medical policy that defines Medical Necessity as adopted by BCBSNC. The term “Medical Necessity” is found in all standard BCBSNC certificates. Definitions for non-standard certificates may vary. As used herein, a service includes, but is not limited to a diagnostic service, procedure, test, treatment, facility, equipment, drug or device. Policy BCBSNC will provide reimbursement for services when BCBSNC determines that the medical criteria and guidelines defining “Medical Necessity” are met as described in this Corporate Medical Policy, provided that coverage is available under the Member’s BCBSNC health benefit plan. Benefits Application This medical policy relates only to the services described herein. Please refer to the Member's Benefit Booklet for availability of benefits. Member's benefits may vary according to benefit design; therefore member benefit language should be reviewed before applying the terms of this medical policy. If BCBSNC determines that a Service does not meet the definition of Medical Necessity, it will not be covered. The fact that a doctor may prescribe, order, recommend, or approve a service does not, in and of itself, mean that that service meets the definition of “Medical Necessity.” Only the Member’s medical condition is considered when deciding which setting (i.e., inpatient or outpatient) or service is medically necessary. This policy applies to all product lines of business unless otherwise indicated. Note: BCBSNC does not cover investigational, cosmetic, or other services that do not meet the definition of Medical Necessity and will not reimburse them. Definition of Medical Necessity All of the following criteria must be met for a service to be determined to be a Medical Necessity: Service is provided for the diagnosis, treatment, cure, or relief of a health condition, illness, injury, or disease, AND Service is not for experimental, investigational, or cosmetic purposes except as allowed under North Carolina G.S. 58-3-255, AND Service is necessary for and appropriate to the diagnosis, treatment, cure, or relief of a health condition, illness, injury, disease, or its symptoms, AND Service is within generally accepted standards of medical care in the community, AND Service is not solely for the convenience of the insured, the insured's family, or the provider. For these purposes, “generally accepted standards of medical practice” means standards that are based on credible scientific evidence published in peer-reviewed medical literature that is generally recognized by the relevant medical community, physician specialty society recommendations, and the views of physicians practicing in relevant clinical areas and any other relevant factors. BCBSNC may compare the cost-effectiveness of alternative services or supplies when determining which of the services or supplies will be covered and/or the setting in which medically necessary services are eligible for coverage. Policy Guidelines Not Applicable Billing/Coding/Physician Documentation Information This policy may apply to the following codes. Inclusion of a code in this section does not guarantee that it will be reimbursed. For further information on reimbursement guidelines, please see Administrative Policies on the Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Carolina web site at www.bcbsnc.com. They are listed in the Category Search on the Medical Policy search page. Applicable service codes: See procedure code for specific procedure or service. BCBSNC may request medical records for determination of Medical Necessity. When medical records are requested, letters of support and/or explanation are often useful but are not sufficient documentation unless all specific information needed to make a Medical Necessity determination is included.   "criteria_quotes": [
    "The publicly available Blue Cross NC policy titled \"Medical Necessity\" states that all of the following criteria must be met: \"Service is provided for the diagnosis, treatment, cure, or relief of a health condition, illness, injury, or disease\"; \"Service is not for experimental, investigational, or cosmetic purposes\"; \"Service is necessary for and appropriate to the diagnosis, treatment, cure, or relief of a health condition, illness, injury, disease, or its symptoms\"; \"Service is within generally accepted standards of medical care in the community\"; and \"Service is not solely for the convenience of the insured, the insured's family, or the provider.\"",
    "The publicly available Blue Cross NC Medical Necessity policy says that generally accepted standards are based on \"credible scientific evidence published in peer-reviewed medical literature,\" relevant physician-specialty recommendations, the views of physicians practicing in relevant clinical areas, and other relevant factors."
  ],
  "appeal_deadline": "2027-02-19. Blue Cross NC states that a member appeal must be received within 180 days of the date on the adverse benefit determination or denial letter. The supplied letter gives the same deadline.",

    "method": "Complete the Blue Cross NC Member Appeal Form and include the reference/authorization number, the reason for appeal, and supporting medical records or other documentation.",

  },
  "how_to_obtain_criteria": "No publicly accessible Blue Cross NC document was found containing CPT 28296-specific medical-necessity criteria. Blue Cross NC publicly states that commercial medical-necessity decisions are guided by MCG Health evidence-based care guidelines and Blue Cross NC corporate medical policy. The MCG criteria are not publicly available on the pages retrieved. Request from Blue Cross NC, using the customer-service number on the member ID card, a copy of the exact MCG guideline, version/date, any Blue Cross NC customization, and all clinical criteria applied to reference POC-BA397EFDB1-13824. Also ask the treating provider to obtain the criteria through Blue Cross NC's provider resources; Blue Cross NC search results state that non-public guidelines can be viewed through the MCG Cite Guideline Transparency Portal.",
